answer.rationale: Current data shows onboarding completion and activation both declining QoQ. Two memories directly support onboarding simplification as effective: memory_86 documented that shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, and memory_31 showed that signup field reduction produced durable first-week activation lift in SMB segments. Both are directly applicable to reversing the 4% onboarding decline and 6% activation decline. While promotional_pricing could address competitive pressure, memory_73 warns it materially harms 30-day retention and violates our primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue. Activation_messaging is promising but less direct given we already have baseline evidence of onboarding friction. Referral_incentive targets established customers, not addressing the current acquisition-phase problem. Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the self-serve SMB activation challenge. Verification of memory_86 and memory_31 will confirm effect sizes and any confounding variables before committing to a standard-scale experiment that tightens onboarding flows.
